The npm builder accepts shared module/export selection, `arities`, `specializations`, `hostProjections`, `contracts`, `generators`, `targets.npm.name`, and `targets.npm.version`. The CPAN projection also accepts `resources`, `arities`, `targets.cpan.module`, and `targets.cpan.version`. [Ordinary C/C++ builds](../publish/c.md#build-an-ordinary-lean-project) accept the shared configuration for pure copied primitive signatures and use `targets.c.name`/`version` and `targets.cpp.name`/`version`. C-only builds do not require CPAN settings or Perl tools. [PHP-Wasm](../publish/php.md#build-an-ordinary-php-wasm-package) separates `targets.php-wasm.npm.name`/`version` from `targets.php-wasm.composer.name`/`version`. Repeat `--target` to combine supported targets from one captured source tree, with one compilation per ABI. The [staged implementation](../architecture/cross-language-authoring.md) tracks the remaining type-family decisions. A reviewed Binding IR owns its export decisions; only `modules`, exact `hostProjections`, package metadata, generators and target settings can accompany it.

### Select an explicit host-null projection

`hostProjections` authorizes an exact Lean wrapper and its two constructors; it
does not infer nullability from a name or from `Option`. Each entry has `name`,
`nullConstructor`, and `valueConstructor`, all fully qualified Lean names. The
array contains at most 32 entries.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "modules": ["NullableApi"],
  "exports": ["NullableApi.echo"],
  "hostProjections": [{
    "name": "NullableApi.HostNull",
    "nullConstructor": "NullableApi.HostNull.null",
    "valueConstructor": "NullableApi.HostNull.value"
  }],
  "targets": {
    "php-wasm": {
      "npm": { "name": "nullable-api-wasm", "version": "1.0.0" },
      "composer": { "name": "nullable-api/wasm", "version": "1.0.0" }
    }
  }
}
```

The wrapper must be unary and generic. The null constructor takes no payload;
the value constructor takes exactly the wrapper's type argument. Compiler-backed
analysis authenticates those declarations and every selected use before any
adapter is emitted. Source-only discovery rejects the selection because it
cannot authenticate constructors.

Keep this field when building an independently reviewed Binding IR. The review
describes `host-null` in the public type graph, while the configuration supplies
the exact Lean names that fresh compilation must reproduce. Do not copy the
constructor names into ordinary Option metadata. See [Choose an export
shape](export-decisions.md#select-an-explicit-host-null-wrapper) for semantics
and the [PHP guide](../php.md#explicit-host-null) for its consumer values.

### Select an explicit host-null wrapper

Use a host-null projection only when the public API deliberately gives one Lean
constructor the meaning “host null.” Keep it distinct from `Option`, `Unit`, an
omitted argument, a default and an unsupported value. For example:

```lean
inductive HostNull (α : Type u) where
  | null
  | value (value : α)

def echo (value : HostNull UInt32) : HostNull UInt32 := value
```

Authorize the exact generic wrapper and both constructors in
`lean-bridge.exports.json`:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "modules": ["NullableApi"],
  "exports": ["NullableApi.echo"],
  "hostProjections": [{
    "name": "NullableApi.HostNull",
    "nullConstructor": "NullableApi.HostNull.null",
    "valueConstructor": "NullableApi.HostNull.value"
  }],
  "targets": {
    "npm": { "name": "nullable-api", "version": "1.0.0" },
    "php-native": { "name": "nullable-api/php", "version": "1.0.0" }
  }
}
```

Lean Bridge compiles fresh metadata and requires a unary generic wrapper with
exactly the selected nullary and unary constructors. A matching name is not
enough. The same selection accompanies an independently reviewed Binding IR;
fresh Lean must reproduce the wrapper, constructors and every selected use.
The private Binding IR records the `host-null` type constructor but does not
turn constructor names into a host-authored ABI claim.

The selected null constructor becomes the host language's null value and the
value constructor becomes its payload. The payload must itself have a
representation distinct from null. Nested `HostNull (Option T)` and
`Option (HostNull T)` therefore retain three distinct states instead of
collapsing either `Option.none` into null. JavaScript/TypeScript and the PHP
profiles have installed package acceptance for copied parameters, results,
fields and synchronous callback positions. Other targets require their own
installed evidence; selecting a target never silently drops this distinction.

### Explicit host null

A publisher may select one exact two-constructor Lean wrapper as a host-null
projection. In that package only, the selected null constructor crosses as PHP
`null`, while its value constructor crosses as the payload directly. Lean
Bridge does not infer this behavior from a type name, an unsupported value, a
proof, `Unit`, `Option.none`, an omitted argument or a default.

The package uses generated `None` and `Some` classes for every Lean `Option` so
host null and option absence cannot collapse into the same PHP value:

| Lean value | PHP value |
| --- | --- |
| `HostNull.null : HostNull UInt32` | `null` |
| `HostNull.value 42` | Native: `42`; PHP-Wasm: `BigInteger::of(42)` |
| `HostNull.null : HostNull (Option UInt32)` | `null` |
| `HostNull.value none` | `new None()` |
| `HostNull.value (some 42)` | `new Some(42)` or, in PHP-Wasm, `new Some(BigInteger::of(42))` |
| `none : Option (HostNull UInt32)` | `new None()` |
| `some HostNull.null` | `new Some(null)` |

For example, a generated package namespace `LeanNullable` can preserve all
three states without a side channel:

```php
use LeanNullable\{None, Some};
use function LeanNullable\{nullable_option, optional_nullable};

$outerNull = nullable_option(null);          // HostNull.null
$innerNone = nullable_option(new None());    // HostNull.value Option.none
$presentNull = optional_nullable(new Some(null)); // Option.some HostNull.null
```

The same mapping applies to copied parameters, results, record fields,
synchronous callback parameters and synchronous callback results in native PHP
and PHP-Wasm packages. Invalid branch objects or payloads reject before Lean
entry, and a later valid call still works. A selected HostNull payload must have
a PHP representation distinct from `null`; for example, a publisher cannot
project `HostNull Unit` through this direct representation.

Publishers configure this projection with the exact Lean wrapper and constructor
names in `hostProjections`; consumers do not configure it. The generated API,
PHPDoc and package README show whether a prepared release uses the tagged Option
representation.
